title: How Tibo sold Tweet Hunter and Taplio for $10M+, then tripled ARR and bought Typeframe
summary: Tibo explains why he sold two platform-dependent SaaS products, how revenue tripled after the sale by shipping more and running yearly challenges, and why lean teams, DM-based support and shipping messy content work. He also covers buying Typeframe with a revenue-share deal and managing AI and platform risk.

principles.text: Ship more across features, SEO and social. Most experiments fade, but a few win big.
principles.quote: My strategy right now with Tom is do a lot. I really do more, ship more in terms of feature, SEO contents, social media contents. And the thing is a lot of those are fading, but a few of them are succeeding in very big ways.

principles.text: Recurring annual campaigns tied to user motivation (like New Year growth challenges) can become a reliable acquisition engine.
principles.quote: for every new year, just tell themselves this year is going to be the year where I'm going to be serious about Twitter or serious about LinkedIn. And we are trying to help them like motivate them on a daily basis

principles.text: Keep the team lean so you can go from idea to live without layers of approval.
principles.quote: we have always remained very lean with the team. And I think that's a part of what makes us go very fast.

principles.text: As a small founder, be directly reachable. Fast fixes from real-time DM support impress users and improve the product.
principles.quote: we're redirecting people to my own Twitter DMS. And so I got the DM in real time ... I was able to listen, see a feedback and try to implement the fix in like five minutes.

principles.text: Start with messy content and ship consistently. Quantity leads to quality, and you improve by living with the shame of shipping.
principles.quote: I'm a big believer of like, quantity leads to quality

principles.text: Buy stalled products with a revenue-share deal, then convert them to subscriptions to grow fast.
principles.quote: I switched it to a subscription based products. And from September to December, we went from zero to 4k in monthly recurring revenue.
